newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - ADT rejects new Western Resources bid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - ADT rejects new Western Resources bid.

text.p: ADT Ltd. rejected a takeover offer by Western Resources Inc. on Monday just a few hours after the Kansas utility revised its $3.5 billion bid.
The rejection marked the second time the electronic security giant has rejected an unsolicited offer from its largest shareholder.
ADT said it will recommend its shareholders reject the hostile offer as inadequate, as it does not reflect the inherent value of the company.

Earlier Monday, the Topeka, Kan.-based utility revised its $22.50 cash and stock offer to raise the cash portion of the bid by 33 percent. The offer now consists of $10 in cash and $12.50 in stock for each ADT share. The original offer was for $7.50 in cash and $15 in Western stock.
Western, which owns 27.1 percent of ADT, said the new bid reflected the fact that ADT is slated to receive $77.5 million in cash from a recent lawsuit settlement.
In a letter to ADT Chairman Michael Ashcroft, Western Chairman John Hayes urged a meeting between the companies to "discuss a mutually beneficial combination of Western Resources and ADT."
Ashcroft harshly dismissed the latest offer as "woefully inadequate", saying the company's board would even reject an all-cash offer of $22.50 per share.

"I think all that Western has done today is tinker with what is a woefully inadequate bid. All that Western has done today is rearrange the deck chairs on the Titanic," he said in a telephone interview.

In reacting to ADT's rejection, Western said it was disappointed by the "knee-jerk reaction" and would proceed with its takeover attempt. Western also said it would sell ADT's auto-auction business if successful in the acquisition, and expected to realize $450 million from the sale.
ADT, which previously had announced its intent to sell the business, said it expects to complete a transaction in the second quarter.

ADT, based in Bermuda, also said Western would not make a strong strategic partner and that the merger would offer no strategic opportunities for ADT or its shareholders. Instead, it would produce unacceptable risks for all ADT stakeholders, it said.

"We understand why a slow growth Kansas utility thinks it would benefit from buying a high growth international electronic security services company but fail to see any compelling reason why ADT shareholders would benefit from such an alliance," Ashcroft said.

ADT said its Security Services division is evolving into a company which gathers and distributes data for premises control services, and is positioning itself for significant growth in a rapidly changing industry.
ADT has scheduled a special general meeting for July 8 to vote on Western's proposals to replace its directors with ADT employees. It has filed a preliminary proxy statement opposing that proposal.
ADT, meanwhile, is suing former banker and financial adviser Chase Manhattan Corp., charging it with breach of fiduciary duty for assisting Western in its hostile bid.
ADT stock rose 12.5 cents to $21.875 on the New York Stock Exchange, while Western Resources gained 25 cents to $30.50.
